videos.title: Do they know that we know that they know?
videos.description: In this video, we talk about AI scheming. In particular, we walk through a study in which OpenAI and Apollo Research tested whether AI models would take "covert actions": strategically withholding, misrepresenting, or concealing information.  The researchers gave two reasoning models a series of challenges to test their propensity to scheme, then tested whether a technique called "deliberative alignment" could reduce this behavior. The results were promising, but came with a complication: models sometimes realized they were being tested, which made them behave better.  The video also covers a strange result from the study: the models' chains of thought often contained unusual words and phrases used in inexplicable ways.  ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀SOURCES & READINGS▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀  Main source:  Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training https://www.antischeming.ai/  Additional sources:  Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models https://arxiv.org/html/2509.13333v1  Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23836v3  Claude Sonnet 4.5 System Card, section on evaluation awareness https://assets.anthropic.com/m/12f214efcc2f457a/original/Claude-Sonnet-4-5-System-Card.pdf#h.gvrj5j7ae3m3  Further readings:  Testing Gemini models for scheming tendencies https://deepmindsafetyresearch.medium.com/testing-gemini-models-for-scheming-tendencies-3368c013ff16  Alignment faking in large language models https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14093  Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05566  Chain of Thought Monitorability: A New and Fragile Opportunity for AI Safety https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11473  ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀PATREON, MEMBERSHIP, MERCH▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀  🟤 Direct donations: https://rationalanimations.com/donate  🟠 Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/rationalanimations  🔵 Channel membership: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCgqt1RE0k0MIr0LoyJRy2lg/join   🟢 Merch: https://rational-animations-shop.fourthwall.com  ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀SOCIAL & DISCORD▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀  Rational Animations Discord: https://discord.gg/5Y3Dwz89yH  Reddit: https://www.reddit.com/r/RationalAnimations/  X/Twitter: https://twitter.com/RationalAnimat1  Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/rationalanimations/  TikTok: https://tiktok.com/@rational.animations  BlueSky: https://bsky.app/profile/rationalanimations.bsky.social  ▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀PATRONS & MEMBERS▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀▀  Thanks to all our patrons and channel members from the Simple Adder tier and above! Whether you are a beginner or preparing for high-stakes tech interviews, this session provides the architectural mindset needed to build scalable applications that handle millions of users.  Course Modules:  Foundations: System Design mindset, Functional vs. Non-Functional Requirements, and Scalability (Vertical vs. Horizontal).  Networking & APIs: Deep dive into DNS, REST APIs, GraphQL, gRPC, and WebSockets.  Data & Storage: SQL vs. NoSQL, Replication, Partitioning (Sharding), and Caching strategies.  Distributed Systems: CAP Theorem, Fault Tolerance, and Observability.  Advanced Topics: Message Queues, Load Balancing algorithms, and real-world Monitoring.  Final Case Study: A full system design walkthrough of a video streaming application.
